answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small, time-locked bond before it may act as a bridge between buyers and sellers: the bond is like a pearl held in escrow, released only after peers attest the agent's work. If an identity misbehaves, its bond is slashed, so creating many fake identities multiplies the attacker's cost linearly, while the delta between honest earnings and attack profit stays negative. Cheap identities become unprofitable, and reputation accrues to bonded, long-lived agents.
